title: Density-Invariant Honest Intervals for a Fixed-Patient Cause-One Competing-Risk Contrast
banked_reason: D0.5 below novelty floor: incremental < field; mathematics and rubric pass, but narrow complete-scale calibration has no usable finite-sample benchmark precision and no supported bounded salvage.
gap_reasons: The delivered novelty is complete-scale inference and quantitative certification for one inherited two-visit pair procedure, a specialized extension rather than a broadly adopted framework.

At the displayed benchmark, finite-sample coverage is supplied by the full-range interval until beyond 10^448 observations; shrinking expected length and Gaussian equivalence are only eventual guarantees.
limitations that competent rewriting cannot repair
proof_attempt_summary: The original matched-minimax angle collided with antecedent work, so the sanctioned second angle developed complete-scale studentization and an all-sample finite-calibration upper theorem for the same two-visit causal contrast. Final mathematics and rubric passed after exact-source attestations and explicit unchanged-score cancellation, but novelty remained incremental: the benchmark Gaussian branch cannot activate before n > 10^448, leaving no demonstrated usable precision. No formalization was entered; useful optimized Bernstein allocation is a separate unproved research program rather than a bounded repair.
tldr: The focal result is a total observable connected interval for the fixed-patient two-visit causal cause-one contrast \(\tau_P(x_0)\): at least \(90\%\) finite-sample coverage over the inherited bounded-design wedge class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{bd}}\), expected length \(O(n^{-r})\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and first-order Hausdorff equivalence to \(I_n^{\mathrm{as}}\). The proof certifies the specified midpoint-frozen sequential score, fitted local Gram, and observable complete scale using bounded-density pair and shared-record counts. Both computation and estimation retain every declared pair. The upper constants do not depend on the optional density exponent \(\xi\), and \(\mathcal P_\xi\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{bd}}\). An internal unaccepted priority artifact studies a related density-invariant risk frontier, pilot architecture, and overlap-only diagnostic. It is not an accepted comparator and is not used to support any theorem here. Novelty is positioned independently against the cited public literature. This note proves a finite-calibration upper theorem and claims no minimax converse or new rate frontier. At the benchmark \(d=2,\gamma=1,\alpha=\eta=\beta=1/6\), the numerical branch cannot activate unless \(n>10^{448}\), and may require more. The certificate therefore establishes no usable finite-sample precision at realistic sample sizes.
gap: Li et al. (2011), supplement Theorem 10(i)--(iii), printed pp.32--33, already supplies uniform conditional higher-order scale estimation and studentization for a global variance-weighted effect. Kennedy et al. (2024), Definition 2 and Theorem 2, pp.15--16 and 24, already supplies localized second-order CATE risk theory. Bladt--Furrer (2025), public Theorem 4.7 and Section 4.3, pp.14--15, and R\"uhl--Friedrich (2024), Section 3.2, p.4, supplies first-order conditional-CIF and average-effect inference. These sourced targets, kernels and hypotheses do not certify the present two-visit frozen-pilot pair score, empirical local Gram and finite full-scale recipe under measurable bounded density.
fill: Theorem 1 certifies the stated pair-square/triple/disjoint-quadruple scale and studentized consequence from finite-history probabilities and bounded-density geometry. De Jong (1987), Theorem 2.1, p.264, supplies the normal-limit principle; normalized fourth moments and fitted-Gram replacement must be derived for this kernel. Theorem 2 applies the established additive bias allowance of Armstrong--Kolesar (2020), Remark 2.2, p.8. Open-ended Question 1 seeks a quantitative finite-sample certificate with the same first-order radius, beyond the risk-calibrated interval in the internal CIF bank.
